summary: DoH-enabled browsers bypass split-DNS while VPN active, causing internal TLS handshake failures
description: Issue summary: Several staff on macOS + Chrome/Firefox connected to office Wi‑Fi then VPN report that internal web services (https://internal-api.redwood.local and https://console.private.redwood) intermittently fail TLS handshake verification. Impact: Developers cannot access internal dashboards and kubectl over local proxies; some CI jobs triggered from local machines fail. Initial pattern shows browser-level failures (ERR_CERT_COMMON_NAME_INVALID or TLS handshake timeout) while curl against the same host from the same machine sometimes succeeds. Hypothesis is that DoH in-browser is bypassing corporate split-DNS while the OS resolver points internal names to private IPs over the VPN.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Join corporate Wi‑Fi (sf-office-1) and start company VPN (IKEv2 client v4.3.1)
2) Confirm /etc/resolv.conf points to 10.10.0.2 (vpn-resolver) for search domain redwood.local
3) Open Chrome (with DoH enabled by default on this build) and navigate to https://internal-api.redwood.local
4) Observe TLS error or certificate mismatch in browser, while 'curl --resolve internal-api.redwood.local:443:10.10.12.34 https://internal-api.redwood.local' succeeds
5) Disable browser DoH (or toggle to use system resolver) and reload; page loads normally in all tested cases.
observed_behavior: Browsers with built-in DoH resolve internal hostnames to public DNS records (public-facing CDN hostname) instead of the private VPN IP. This leads to TLS hostname mismatch or routing to the wrong endpoint. Intermittent because some client caches and network timing cause different resolvers to be used per request.
expected_behavior: When VPN is active and the OS resolver points to the corporate split-DNS, browsers should respect the OS resolver for private names or we should force DoH to use the enterprise resolver so internal hostnames resolve to private addresses and TLS validation succeeds.
logs: Mar 12 10:23:14 chrome[4215]: ResolveJob for internal-api.redwood.local -> 52.8.122.18 (public CDN) via DoH

Mar 12 10:24:02 curl: Connected to 10.10.12.34 port 443 (#0)
  TLS handshake: success
investigation_notes: Support triage: reproduced with developer laptop (macOS 12.6.4) and latest Chrome. Disabling DoH in browser fixed page load immediately.
Network: VPN pushes 10.10.0.2 as DNS resolver and search domain redwood.local. OS resolver confirms private records for internal-api.redwood.local -> 10.10.12.34.
Security: Certificate presented by 52.8.122.18 is valid for public CDN name, causing CN mismatch for internal hostname.

Hypothesis: Modern browsers use DoH by default and choose a public DoH endpoint (Cloudflare/Google) bypassing OS split-DNS; when DoH returns public record, traffic goes to public endpoint and TLS fails for internal name.
Workaround observation: Chrome policy 'DnsOverHttpsMode' set to 'off' returns to system resolver; alternatively set 'DnsOverHttpsTemplates' to enterprise DoH endpoint.
Scope: ~12 engineers reported in #it-support; affected when using Chrome/Firefox with default settings. Safari (system resolver) not impacted.
Related: INT-1234567 showed WSL DoH issues; INT-927413 multi-homing tickets showed asymmetric resolution can cause similar session resets.
temporary_workaround: 1) Instruct users to disable browser DoH or configure browser to use the enterprise DoH template (policy) until a permanent fix is rolled out.
2) Recommend using curl with --resolve or using 'dig @10.10.0.2' to verify private A record before connecting.
3) For macOS, updating Chrome policies via MDM to set DnsOverHttpsMode = 'off' for corporate devices provides immediate relief.
4) Network workaround option: advertise an enterprise DoH resolver reachable while VPN is active and publish policy to browsers via GPO/MDM.
resolution_plan: Short term (1-2 days): Publish MDM policy to set DnsOverHttpsMode='off' for managed macOS devices; communicate to staff and provide quick steps for BYOD.
Mid term (1-3 weeks): Stand up a tenant-scoped enterprise DoH endpoint (ldns.redwood.local) inside the VPN and push DnsOverHttpsTemplates to managed browsers so DoH queries respect split-DNS.
Long term (1-2 months): Engage product/security to update onboarding docs and MDM baseline to enforce browser resolver policy; update runbooks for new browser versions that enable DoH by default.
Owners: Network (Priyanka Rao) to provision DoH endpoint; Security (Omar Ruiz) to approve; Endpoint/MDM (Liam Chen) to push policy; Support (Aisha Patel) to communicate.
Follow-ups: Create a postmortem entry and update incident KB referencing this ticket.
resolution: In progress: MDM policy drafted, awaiting security approval. Enterprise DoH staging env provisioned and smoke-tested internally. Full rollout scheduled after approvals.
